packets.story: Everything agrees: species, part, area, dates inside the authorisation window, quantities within the authorised amount, and the drying mass balance closes.
Collection on 12 Sep 2026 (written day-first) happened after the authorisation expired on 30 Jun 2026.
The authorisation uses the synonym Nardostachys grandiflora (fine, flagged for information); the weigh-in names a different plant, Valeriana jatamansi.
Leaves are authorised but bark was collected.
Two slips (one in grams) add up to 62 kg against 50 kg authorised.
The plan targets Block C; the authorisation covers Block A.
The batch statement refers to lot JAT-D9, which no collection or drying record produced.
The same weigh-in slip was submitted twice; counting both would double the stock.
80 kg fresh in, 21 kg dry out, only 40 kg water loss recorded: 19 kg unaccounted.
Loss on drying 14.2% exceeds the documented 12% limit; total ash was not tested. Pages are in reverse order.
A CITES Appendix II species is invoiced to France; trade documents need checking by the Management Authority. The authorisation is in French.
One file is damaged and must be rejected; one is an image-only scan, where the system must abstain rather than guess.

HELD-OUT: same facts as P05 (55 kg collected, 40 kg authorised) but with unseen labels. Measures what the rules extractor misses on a new layout; missed fields should lead to abstention, not a false 'consistent'.
